title: Batch Conductor: continuous workload fingerprinting, heuristic mixer, and guarded parameter roll-forward
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a continuous 'Batch Conductor' service that generates conservative batching and caching parameter proposals per workload, evaluates them in shadow mode, and performs guarded roll-forward with automatic rollback triggers. The conductor combines three subsystems: (1) a fingerprinting pipeline that maintains compact workload signatures over time, (2) a heuristic mixer that creates candidate parameter vectors from multi-signal objectives (latency SLO, per-token cost, error/quality delta, KV cache hit-rate), and (3) a safe-apply controller that stages candidates via shadow coalescing, canary traffic, and runbook-enabled automatic rollback. This ticket covers the end-to-end MVP including telemetry, staged rollout automation, and operator controls in Console.
background: Current batching tuning is manual and reactive: SEs examine histograms and create static config patches. We see missed opportunities for coalescing and inconsistent cache-friendly prefixes. Several infra incidents (latency regressions after naive large-batch applies) highlighted the need for safer automation. The Batch Conductor is intended to reduce unit cost while preserving latency SLOs and quality, and to provide explainable parameter proposals for operator review.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor produces workload fingerprints and stores them in profiles (compact signature + recent histograms)
Heuristic mixer emits candidate parameter vectors (max_batch_tokens, coalesce_window_ms, kv_prefix_shard, latency_target_ms) with expected cost/latency delta estimates
Shadow-run harness executes candidates on a shadow copy of traffic and records latency, error, and cache metrics for 24h
Safe-apply controller can roll candidates to 1%, 5%, 25% traffic with automated rollback conditions (latency > SLO + 10% p95, error-rate increase > 2x baseline, cost increase above expected by 15%)
Console displays per-workload proposal rationale and a diff view with telemetry links and PR link to configuration change
Unit/integration tests covering fingerprint drift detector, mixer scoring function, and rollback triggers exist and pass in CI
technical_design: Fingerprinting: lightweight sliding-window signatures built from sequence-length distribution, KV prefix entropy, inter-arrival statistics, and recent token count per request. Store sketches in time-series store and compact snapshots into per-workload profiles. Heuristic Mixer: ensemble of rules and learned weightings. Rules cover conservative heuristics (never exceed KV-safe batch size), cost-first heuristics for batch-heavy workloads, and latency-first heuristics for latency-sensitive workloads. Mixer outputs candidates with an internal confidence score and predicted deltas estimated via microbench profiles. Shadow-run harness: fork requests to a shadow pool that runs candidate configs under realistic KV cache and memory constraints; use sampling to limit extra GPU load. Safe-apply controller: orchestrates staged rollout with canary percentages, continuous monitors, and a thermostat annealer to gradually increase coalescing window until a measured plateau. Rollback: deterministic triggers based on multi-signal synthesis; operator can force-commit or abort. All controller actions are logged and produce a GitOps-style patch (linkable PR) for audit and rollback. Telemetry: produce aggregated KPIs (unit_cost_change, p50/p95 latency delta, cache_hit_delta, quality_eval_score) and traces linked to request IDs.
rollout_steps: Phase 0: internal dry-run using replayed production traces against an isolated cluster
Phase 1: shadow-run on 0.1% live sampled traffic for one workload cohort (non-critical customers)
Phase 2: extend shadow-run to 5 workloads and run 48h statistical comparison
Phase 3: canary apply for a single workload (1% -> 5% -> 25%), monitor for 72h with automatic rollback triggers enabled
Phase 4: bulk rollout to low-risk workloads with operator approval and automated gradual scaling
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprinting sketch and mixer scoring. Integration tests: shadow-run simulation harness using synthetic traces and latency injectors. Load tests: run candidate configs on staging cluster with representative KV cache behavior. Canary verification: automated checks that replicate rollback conditions and successful gradational increases. Add golden evaluators to detect hallucination/quality regressions using the existing eval harness (link to eval sets).
implementation_notes: Start with a conservative default policy that prioritizes p95 latency. Implement mixer as modular pipeline so we can add learned models later. Ensure all changes produce a human-readable rationale string for Console UI. Implement safety knobs: max_adjust_per_day, min_cache_preserve_ratio, emergency-disable-flag. Use existing rollout library for gradual traffic shifts and reuse tracing hooks for shadow runs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shadow runs may not accurately represent production cache behavior -> Mitigation: model KV cache state in shadow pool and validate with synthetic cache warmup
Risk: Over-aggressive batch expansion could cause OOMs -> Mitigation: conservative upper bounds and preflight memory check
Risk: Quality regressions (increased hallucination) -> Mitigation: integrate eval harness and require explicit quality gating for any candidate that changes tokenization or quantization profiles
updates: 2026-01-12: Kickoff meeting. Agreed scope for MVP: fingerprinting + mixer + shadow-run + canary apply. Owners assigned.
2026-01-22: Prototype fingerprint sketches implemented (sparse histograms + reservoir sampling). Initial unit tests added. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/248
2026-01-30: Mixer rule-set drafted. Conservative-first policy defined. Need to decide on learned-weight update cadence (weekly vs. daily).

2026-02-05: Shadow-run harness integrated with tracing. First internal dry-run completed against 7 days of replayed traces. Observed 6-8% unit cost reduction for batch-friendly cohort with no latency regression in dry-run. Moving to limited live shadow runs next sprint.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on mixer scoring (is confidence well-calibrated?), rollback trigger thresholds, and telemetry coverage. Ops should validate the emergency-disable plan. PM: confirm acceptance criteria align with product risk tolerance for automated actions.
